title: FNIP1 variants are associated with favourable metabolism in 1 million humans.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed Hindy_et_al_TGHDLratio_Rare_Variant_Gene_Level_Results.tsv.gz (1.1 MB) from the Regeneron Genetics Center (RGC) portal: 19,467 rows x 11 columns, 0 missing values, 0 duplicate genes, Ensembl IDs embedded in the Name column, 60 genes at P < 1.04e-7 and 140 at P < 1e-4; APOC3, APOB, ANGPTL3, LPL, ANGPTL4 rank at the top and FNIP1 has P = 2.9e-10, effect -0.48 SD. Read the README (every column documented, units = SD of rank-normalised TG:HDL ratio, GRCh38). The download sits behind a click-through licence page (JavaScript button, no login); the files are fetched directly. HEAD only on the common-variant file (207 MB, not downloaded). Opened GEO GSE330407 counts: 32,422 mouse genes x 20 samples (liver Flcn knockout).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That individual-level data from UK Biobank, MCPS, GHS and other cohorts need access applications; the 1,032,116 sample size and ancestry mix; that 59 genes are 'independent' (the file has 60 at the threshold before conditioning); the hepatocyte and mouse experiments. Supplementary tables were not retrievable (Europe PMC supplementaryFiles timed out).

a1_downloadable.note: Gene-level burden results download directly after a click-through licence page, no account (checked). The individual-level cohort data are controlled access (UK Biobank, GHS, MCPS etc.), so only summary statistics are usable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The label is already a column: PValue_Cauchy (gene-level p-value combined across 24 burden masks) and Effect (beta in SD units for the best mask). Seen in the file.

a3_inputs_present.note: The table holds no gene features; inputs must come from one bulk join on the Ensembl gene ID (protein sequences, GTEx expression, constraint). It's a single bulk download, not thousands of lookups.

a4_units_stated.note: README states effects are in SD units of inverse-rank-normalised TG:HDL (triglyceride to HDL cholesterol) ratio, GRCh38 coordinates.

a5_enough_rows.note: 19,467 labelled genes (counted), but only 60 pass exome-wide significance and 140 pass P < 1e-4, so the effective number of positives is tiny.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1 MB label table plus ~1-2 GB of protein embeddings/expression features
a6_fits_laptop.note: Gene-level table is trivial; ESM-2 embeddings of ~19k proteins are a one-off CPU job.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper reports 59 independent genes; the file has 60 at P < 1.04e-7 before independence filtering, which is consistent.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label is a regression association statistic from measured blood lipids in ~1M people, not a model prediction. Caveat: which variants enter each mask was chosen using ESM1v and SIFT/PolyPhen predictions, so protein-language-model features share a little information with the label.

B1.why: One clean label table (checked), but every feature must be joined in from GTEx/UniProt on Ensembl ID.

B2.why: TSV parsed first try with pandas, 0 missing values across 11 columns (checked).

B3.why: Single meta-analysis, but Effect comes from a different 'best mask' per gene, so betas aren't strictly comparable.

B4.why: P-values underflow to 0 for APOB/APOC3; log10 column partly rescues it. No other censoring (checked).

B5.why: 0 duplicate gene symbols or names in 19,467 rows (checked).

B6.why: README documents every column, mask code, units and genome build (read).

C1.why: Transfer from smaller UK Biobank burden results to 1M discoveries is informative, but positives are ~60 genes.

C2.why: PoPS and similar gene-prioritisation models are open, but trained on common-variant GWAS, not rare-variant burden labels.

C3.why: Weak unique-application angle: new 1M-exome TG:HDL burden labels for an existing gene-prioritisation task.

C4.why: Exome sequencing of 1M people is very costly; prioritising genes in advance helps only somewhat.

C5.why: Obvious dummies (gene constraint, coding length, liver expression) plus PoPS runnable as a baseline.

D1.why: ESM-2 protein language model, open weights, joinable via Ensembl to UniProt canonical sequences.

D2.why: Mean-pooled ESM-2 embeddings for ~19k proteins cached once on CPU, then a logistic/ridge head.

D3.why: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; RGC data under its own terms-of-use licence (not read in full).

E1.why: Hold out whole chromosomes (Chromosome column present, checked) to stop neighbouring-gene leakage.

E2.why: 23 chromosomes present in the file (checked), enough to hold out groups.

E3.why: Per-gene constraint or liver-expression ranking gives a meaningful dummy baseline.

E4.why: 95% confidence intervals per gene (checked) give per-gene noise; no replicates.

E5.why: Textbook lipid genes (APOC3, ANGPTL3, LPL, APOB) top the file and must rank highest.

E6.why: Label shuffling and feature-block ablation are trivially runnable on a 19k-row table.

E7.why: Genebass UK Biobank exome burden results for TG and HDL are public, though samples overlap.

E8.why: No published ML number exists on this specific gene-level table.

G1.why: Ensembl gene IDs and GRCh38 positions embedded in every row (checked).

G2.why: GTEx expression, Genebass burden results, Open Targets, all keyed on Ensembl gene.

G3.why: One row per gene; collapse to canonical transcript for protein features.

G4.why: Combined question (do gene features anticipate which genes 1M exomes reveal?) is only modestly bigger.

H1.why: All 19,467 genes reported including nulls (checked), not just hits.

H2.why: Multi-ancestry cohorts per paper, but analysis pooled; ancestry proportions not checked.

H4.why: Paper documents cohorts and masks; power limits for short or rare-variant-poor genes are implicit.

I1.why: Human-genetics drug-target groups (e.g. Regeneron Genetics Center) - a community, not a committed user.

I2.why: Could marginally reorder candidate genes for follow-up; unlikely to redirect experiments alone.

I3.why: Precision among top-ranked genes roughly matches a follow-up shortlist decision.

I4.why: Liver expression plus constraint may do nearly as well as any model; ML helps somewhat.

J1.why: Imbalanced classification, grouped splits, frozen embeddings and transfer evaluation.

J2.why: Lipid genetics is well known, so known genes give a sanity check.

J3.why: Feature table plus baseline ranking is shareable even if the model adds nothing.

J4.why: No time budget set yet; roughly one to two weekends.

J5.why: Kill condition proposed below but not yet written in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: PoPS (Polygenic Priority Score), Weeks et al., Nature Genetics 2023
existing_models.score_and_split: Prioritises genes from 57,543 gene features fitted to GWAS summary statistics; paper reports ~74% expected precision for PoPS+local on fine-mapped loci across 113 traits. Not evaluated on rare-variant burden labels at 1M scale.

existing_models.name: DeepRVAT (Nature Genetics 2024), deep set network for rare-variant association
existing_models.score_and_split: More gene discoveries than burden tests on 34 quantitative and 63 binary UK Biobank traits; it is an association test on individual-level data, not a gene-feature predictor.

existing_models.name: FuncRVP (bioRxiv 2024), Bayesian rare-variant risk model using functional gene embeddings
existing_models.score_and_split: Uses gene embeddings as priors for rare-variant effects in UK Biobank; numbers not retrieved.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model, 35M or 150M checkpoint)
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU, ~1-3 h one-off for ~19k canonical proteins

integration.partner_dataset: Genebass (UK Biobank exome burden results, ~394k people) for TG and HDL; GTEx median tissue expression
integration.join_key: Ensembl gene ID (in the Name column)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do gene features plus smaller-cohort burden results predict which genes only become significant once exome sample size reaches 1 million?

controls.positive_control: APOC3, ANGPTL3, LPL, APOB, ANGPTL4 must rank in the top 1% of predictions; liver expression should be enriched among hits.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle gene labels within chromosome and confirm precision-at-k collapses to the base rate (60/19,467).
controls.external_validation: Genebass UK Biobank burden results for triglycerides and HDL (overlapping samples, so not fully independent).

honest_claim_h3: Among ~19,500 protein-coding genes, the model ranks which ones carry detectable rare coding-variant association with TG:HDL ratio in a pooled 1M-exome meta-analysis, where detectability also depends on gene length and how many rare damaging variants exist.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gene properties (protein sequence, tissue expression, intolerance to mutation) to predict which genes' rare damaging variants shift the blood triglyceride-to-HDL ratio.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per human gene with features joined from protein sequence and expression atlases; 19,467 genes in the verified table.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the gene has a significant rare-variant association (and its direction and size) with TG:HDL ratio, measured by regression of blood lipid levels on carrier status in ~1M sequenced people.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Tells target-discovery groups whether a cheap gene-level model could have flagged genes like FNIP1 before a million exomes were sequenced; a failure shows rare-variant hits aren't predictable from gene annotation.

more_or_better_data.why: Labels come from 1,032,116 exomes versus ~394k in Genebass UK Biobank, but PoPS-style models train on GWAS signals across many traits, so ours is one trait with only 60 significant genes.

confidence_score.why: Per-gene 95% confidence intervals allow weighting labels by certainty; whether PoPS reports per-gene calibrated confidence was not checked.

models_beatable.why: PoPS (2023) is a linear model on hand-built features without a pretrained protein backbone, but it is open and well evaluated; beating it on 60 positives would be statistically shaky.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Genebass burden results overlap the same UK Biobank samples and use different masks, so the new data does not measure the same quantity the same way on an independent split.

label_elsewhere.sources: Genebass (UK Biobank exome burden results across thousands of phenotypes including lipids) and the AstraZeneca PheWAS portal - known resources, not opened here.
label_elsewhere.why: Gene-level burden labels for many related traits would allow multi-trait pretraining and an external check, though cohorts overlap with this meta-analysis.

risks: Neighbouring genes in the same locus (e.g. APOA1/APOC3/APOA5 cluster) share signal, so splitting genes randomly leaks locus information.
Masks were defined using ESM1v deleteriousness, so ESM-based features partly encode which variants were counted.
Gene length and number of rare variants drive statistical power, so a model may learn power, not biology.
Genebass validation labels come from UK Biobank, which is also inside the 1M meta-analysis.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole chromosomes using the Chromosome column (seen in the file, 23 values), with paralog families kept on one side.
checks: Shuffle labels within chromosome and confirm precision-at-100 drops to the 0.3% base rate.
Train on coding length and variant count alone to measure how much is statistical power.
Compare ESM-2 features with and without the ESM1v-defined masks' genes to check mask leakage.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable: chromosome hold-out handles locus leakage, but the power confound needs an explicit length/variant-count baseline.

success_criteria.metric: Precision among the top 100 ranked genes on held-out chromosomes, because a follow-up team would examine a short list.
success_criteria.baselines: Base rate 60/19,467 = 0.31% (computed); liver-expression and gene-constraint rankings (not yet computed); PoPS scores for lipid traits if available.
success_criteria.success: Top-100 precision at least twice that of the best single-feature baseline on held-out chromosomes; exact numbers unknown until baselines are computed.
success_criteria.kill: If the model adds under 0.05 PR-AUC (precision-recall area under the curve) over a coding-length plus liver-expression logistic regression after one weekend, stop.

ambitious.why: Publishes rare-variant gene discovery methods; would need the model to anticipate new 1M-scale hits across several traits, not just TG:HDL.

realistic.why: A short benchmark of gene-feature models against rare-variant burden labels fits its application notes.

fallback.why: A negative result that rare-variant hits are explained by power plus liver expression is still a citable note.

pitch.headline: A clean 19,467-gene table of rare-variant TG:HDL associations from 1,032,116 exomes, downloadable without login.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Gene-level burden results at 1M-exome scale with 0 missing values, Ensembl IDs, confidence intervals and 60 exome-wide-significant genes including new hits like FNIP1 (P = 2.9e-10).
pitch.the_win: A frozen protein-embedding model ranking known plus newly discovered TG:HDL genes in the top 100 on held-out chromosomes at clearly above length/expression baselines.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We learn whether rare-variant discoveries are just statistical power plus liver expression, which says gene-level ML adds little to target discovery.
pitch.who_wants_it: Human-genetics target-discovery groups such as the Regeneron Genetics Center, deciding which genes to prioritise before the next sequencing round.

ml_idea: Join the RGC gene-level burden table to ESM-2 protein embeddings, GTEx expression and constraint by Ensembl ID; train a class-weighted logistic/ridge head to rank genes by TG:HDL burden signal with chromosome hold-out, benchmarked against coding-length, expression and PoPS baselines, and test transfer from Genebass UK Biobank lipid burden labels.

effort.compute_note: Estimated: ~19k proteins through ESM-2 35M on CPU at a few proteins per second; a logistic head on 19k x 480 features cross-validates in minutes. Nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Fit logistic regression on coding length plus liver expression alone and see how many of the 60 significant genes land in its top 100; if most do, the ML project is a one-page note.

verdict_reason: The open gene-level table is clean and model-ready (19,467 genes, checked), but it has only ~60 positive genes for one trait, and gene-prioritisation models like PoPS already exist, so the likely result is a marginal benchmark. Individual-level data are controlled access.
